subject: Foray #1 — grilling & world barbecue
purpose: Prioritised ASR work order. Every row is an episode measured ad-free that we want a timed transcript for. Sorted by value per minute of CPU: an episode that fills an EMPTY arc slot outranks one that adds depth to a filled one.
companions: docs/curation/catalogue-broadening.md — where the new sources came from, and which traditions stayed unsourceable
docs/curation/grilling-foray-passages.md — the 8 passages that already exist (8:21)
committed_here_because: docs/curation/ carries no source prose — only feed metadata we measured ourselves — and data-local/ is gitignored, so a manifest placed there would be invisible to every other checkout and to cloud runners. Same call as docs/curation/grilling-foray-passages.json.

method.ad_free_ratio: delivered bytes / feed-declared enclosure length, via a 2-byte ranged GET reading the true total from Content-Range (tools/transcribe/ad-inflation.mjs). HEAD lies on ad-inserting hosts and was not used. Threshold < 1.01.
method.true_duration: itunes:duration from the feed, cross-checked against declared_bytes*8/duration landing on a standard bitrate. Rows where the feed declares length=0 or length=1 cannot use the byte method and are labelled bitrate-implied.
method.duration_gaps: None. Every row below carries an itunes:duration read from its feed; there is no row whose true duration could not be obtained.

excluded_by_instruction: The BBQ Central Show — already being transcribed by the American-arc workstream
The British Food History Podcast — already being transcribed
Gastropod — already being transcribed (and measures 1.080, injected)

read_this_before_spending_cpu.language_gate: Every NEW tradition source found in this pass is non-English: Spanish (asado), Portuguese (churrasco), Mandarin (churrasco/yakitori), Korean. The existing 8 passages are all English. Dropping a Spanish or Mandarin segment into an English Foray is a PRODUCT decision (subtitle? narrate over? accept mixed language?), not a transcription decision — and it is unresolved. Rows carry `language` and `english_audio` so the queue can be filtered either way. English-audio priority-1 rows total 8,902 s (2.47 h); non-English priority-1 rows add 3,453 s (0.96 h).
read_this_before_spending_cpu.unfillable_slots: braai, tandoor, mangal/kebab and Filipino lechon have NO source at any transcription budget. See catalogue-broadening.md §4.

totals.cost_note: 1.1x realtime is the figure supplied with this work order, and it assumes an otherwise idle machine. tools/transcribe measured 1.33x for base.en (docs/curation/transcription-scale-plan.md §1); the live whisper queue is currently running at 0.475x because of contention. At 0.475x the same 10.1 hours is 21.3 CPU-hours — roughly a day of laptop. That is the real price of a 3-hour Foray, and it is why the priority ordering matters more than the total: priority 1 alone is 3.12 CPU-hours at 1.1x (7.2 h at 0.475x) and opens five slots that are empty today.

episodes.episode_title: The History of Jerk in Jamaica with Alyssa Sperry Bertrand

If the pipeline can emit word timings against supplied text, this row costs a fraction of full ASR and the same trick unlocks all 8 transcript-bearing Moreish episodes.

episodes.episode_title: # 157 - Clarice Chwartzmann | Churrasqueira / "Cultura e Tradição do Fogo"
episodes.unlocks: churrasco — currently EMPTY, 0:00. NEW FIND from the PodcastIndex bulk dump.
episodes.why_this_priority: The best churrasco source found anywhere: an interview with Clarice Chwartzmann, a gaúcha from Passo Fundo, Rio Grande do Sul, who learned churrasco as a child and whose subject is explicitly 'a cultura e a tradição dos assados e das celebrações ao redor do fogo'. A tradition bearer, not a host reading up. Subject to the language gate above.

episodes.episode_title: El ritual del asado: más que comida, una identidad nacional
episodes.unlocks: asado, from inside the tradition. NEW FIND from the bulk dump.
episodes.why_this_priority: The first Rioplatense asado source this project has found — every asado source before it was American-made. Published by Magnolio Podcast (Uruguay); the episode is explicitly about why asado is part of the cultural DNA of Uruguayans and Argentines, from gaucho roots to the family Sunday. 9:53 of audio, so it is cheap even at 0.475x.
episodes.content_gate: pass on subject, caution on form — single-narrator tips-and-recipes show; this one episode is the cultural/historical entry, the other three are technique.

episodes.episode_title: 百年燒鳥名店的老滷秘密｜Podcast
episodes.ratio_note: The feed declares length="1", so the byte-ratio method cannot run. 11,108,811 bytes over 346 s = 256.9 kbps, i.e. a standard 256 kbps encode with no room for injected inventory. Weaker evidence than a 1.0000 byte ratio — re-check before committing CPU.
episodes.unlocks: yakitori — currently EMPTY, 0:00, and the ONLY explanatory yakitori source found in 4.71M feeds.
episodes.why_this_priority: 5:46 of audio for an otherwise unfillable slot — the cheapest row in the manifest. Content is mechanism, not banter: the tare 'mother pot' kept alive for a century, the preservation and ageing science behind why it does not spoil, and why raw meat never touches the sauce.
episodes.content_gate: pass on substance, caution on provenance — 6-episode SoundOn show with emoji-heavy notes; treat with the same suspicion as Culinary Connections until someone listens.
